claim: NATS-Bench provides a unified tabular search space of 15,625 architecture-topology candidates and 32,768 architecture-size candidates across three datasets, with all candidates trained under an identical setup, specifically to make NAS algorithm comparisons fair and reproducible.
stance_target: the standard for fair, reproducible NAS benchmark comparison that reviewers expect LLM-NAS papers to meet
scope_conditions: topology and size search spaces, three datasets, 13 SOTA NAS algorithms benchmarked
quoted_support: NATS-Bench includes the search space of 15,625 neural cell candidates for architecture topology and 32,768 for architecture size on three datasets... All logs and diagnostic information trained using the same setup for each candidate are provided.

claim: The paper's own motivation identifies that NAS algorithm performance gains are typically achieved under different search spaces and training setups, making overall algorithm performance to some extent incomparable across papers -- the exact confound NATS-Bench was built to remove.
stance_target: the reason tabular benchmarks are demanded by NAS reviewers, per the methodology-standards question
quoted_support: the performance gain from these searching algorithms is achieved under different search spaces and training setups. This makes the overall performance of the algorithms to some extent incomparable and the improvement from a sub-module of the searching model unclear.
